candidates.label: Classic merge-of-K-arithmetic-sequences via a min-heap keyed by (nextFireTime, qnum), popping K times and pushing (time+period, qnum) back each time. NOTE: the stored Sample.output for this problem contains two blank lines in the middle for K=5 with only one dataset in the input, which does not match this straightforward reading of the spec (no multi-dataset separator is implied) -- this looks like a scraping/data artifact rather than a real formatting requirement; flagging for the parent to check the Sample row itself.
Seeds the heap with fire time 0 instead of `period`, so every query incorrectly fires immediately at t=0 instead of waiting Period seconds for its first result.

Tie-break on simultaneous fire times uses `period` instead of `qnum` (tuple ordered (time, period, qnum) rather than (time, qnum, period)) -- only visibly wrong when two queries fire at the exact same time with period not already matching qnum order.
